deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues the previous pages on singular values ρ_1(u) ≥ ρ_2(u) ≥ … of a compact (or finite-rank) operator u: E → F, and on determinant inequalities of Weyl type. Those include (18): ∏(1+ρ_i(u)) = sup |det(1+vu)|.

Step 1 (starting inequality). From the determinantal results of the previous page, Grothendieck takes, for every r ≥ 0 and every n, the inequality ∏_{i≤n}(1+rρ_i(u+v)) ≤ ∏_{i≤n}(1+rρ_i(u)) · ∏_{i≤n}(1+rρ_i(v)). Equivalently A_{u+v}(r) ≤ A_u(r) + A_v(r), with A_u(r) = Σ_{i≤n} log(1+rρ_i(u)) and A(0) = 0. This is a finite-n, Fredholm-determinant form of |det(1+X+Y)| ≤ det(1+|X|)·det(1+|Y|).

Step 2 (the class of functions). For φ ≥ 0 decreasing on (0,∞), he sets f_φ(ρ) = ∫_0^∞ φ(r)/(1/ρ + r) dr = ∫_0^∞ φ(r) ρ/(1+rρ) dr = ∫_0^∞ φ(s/ρ) ds/(1+s). He also sets f_φ^n(u) = Σ_{i≤n} f_φ(ρ_i(u)). Since d/dr log(1+rρ) = ρ/(1+rρ), we get f_φ^n(u) = ∫ φ(r) A_u'(r) dr.

Step 3 (integration-by-parts lemma). Suppose A(0) = B(0) = 0 and A(r) ≤ B(r) for all r. Write φ = ∫ (−dφ), i.e. φ(r) = −∫_r^∞ φ'. Integrating by parts, ∫ φ A' dr = [φA] + ∫ A (−dφ). The boundary terms vanish, so ∫ φA' ≤ ∫ φB' for every decreasing φ ≥ 0 (vanishing near +∞, then by limits).
- Conversely, a step function φ = 1_{[0,a]} gives back A(a) ≤ B(a), so the integrated form is equivalent to the pointwise one.
- If A', B' ≥ 0, the restrictions on φ can be removed by monotone convergence.

Step 4 (conclusion). Taking A = A_{u+v} and B = A_u + A_v gives f_φ^n(u+v) ≤ f_φ^n(u) + f_φ^n(v) for all n and all such φ.

Step 5 (key case, finished on the next page). Take φ(r) = r^{−p} with 0 < p < 1. Then f_φ(ρ) = ρ^p ∫_0^∞ s^{−p}/(1+s) ds = (π/sin pπ) ρ^p. Hence Σ_{i≤n} ρ_i(u+v)^p ≤ Σ_{i≤n} ρ_i(u)^p + Σ_{i≤n} ρ_i(v)^p for every n. In particular S_p(u+v) ≤ S_p(u) + S_p(v): ||·||_p^p is subadditive on the Schatten classes for 0 < p < 1.

The next page then asks for the class of all f for which f^{(n)} is subadditive for every n, and suggests a generalization to functions of several arguments.

Purpose: to control the p-summability (0 < p ≤ 1) of singular values of nuclear-type operators. This serves Grothendieck's theory of Fredholm determinants and the eigenvalue distribution of nuclear and p-summing operators (Produits tensoriels topologiques; La théorie de Fredholm).
errors: The derivative is written A'(r) = Σ r/(1+rρ_i(u)) in the transcription, possibly a slip in the manuscript. The correct derivative is Σ ρ_i(u)/(1+rρ_i(u)), and only this is consistent with the definition of f_φ.

The line 'φ(r) = −φ'(r)' is presumably meant as φ = −ψ' with ψ decreasing, i.e. writing φ as an integral of a positive measure. As written it is confused, but the intended Abel-summation argument is correct.

Boundary terms: A(r) grows like n·log r, so [φA] vanishes at ∞ only if φ(r)·log r → 0. This holds for r^{−p} but needs a limiting argument in general; Grothendieck handles it by first taking φ vanishing near +∞.

Step 1 rests on the determinant inequality ∏_{i≤n}(1+rρ_i(u+v)) ≤ ∏_{i≤n}(1+rρ_i(u))(1+rρ_i(v)), presumably derived on earlier pages from (17)/(18). It is true (it follows from multiplicative majorization of singular values via |det(1+X+Y)| ≤ det(1+|X|)det(1+|Y|)), but it is not proved on this page.

ideas.what: Subadditivity of truncated sums of a function of singular values, Σ_{i≤n} f(s_i(u+v)) ≤ Σ_{i≤n} f(s_i(u)) + Σ_{i≤n} f(s_i(v)), for f(ρ) = ∫ φ(r) ρ/(1+rρ) dr with φ ≥ 0 decreasing.
ideas.modern_name: Rotfel'd inequality (for concave / operator-monotone f with f(0)=0); Thompson / Bourin–Uchiyama inequalities
ideas.usually_credited_to: S. Yu. Rotfel'd (1967–69); R.C. Thompson (1970s); determinant-based proof in Seiler–Simon (1975) and B. Simon's 'Trace Ideals'; Bourin–Uchiyama (2007) for concave f
ideas.where_published: Possibly used implicitly in Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), Ch. II, or 'La théorie de Fredholm' (1956); not known as a stated result there

ideas.what: Proof technique: deduce additive inequalities for a family of concave functions from a one-parameter family of log-determinant inequalities, via the Stieltjes-type representation f(ρ) = ∫ φ(r) d/dr log(1+rρ) dr and Abel summation against decreasing φ.
ideas.modern_name: Integral-representation (operator monotone / Stieltjes function) method for singular-value inequalities

ideas.what: The p-triangle inequality ||u+v||_p^p ≤ ||u||_p^p + ||v||_p^p for Schatten classes with 0<p<1, with its n-truncated form.
ideas.modern_name: Quasi-Banach (p-normed) structure of the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<1
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck uses S_p-type classes for p<1 in Produits tensoriels / Fredholm theory, but an explicit proof of this inequality there is uncertain

ideas.what: Abel/integration-by-parts lemma: A ≤ B pointwise with A(0)=B(0)=0 iff ∫φA' ≤ ∫φB' for all decreasing φ ≥ 0.

missed.claim: The page and the next contain a complete proof, dated around 1953, that Σ_{i≤n} f(s_i(u+v)) ≤ Σ_{i≤n} f(s_i(u)) + Σ_{i≤n} f(s_i(v)) for every f of the form ∫ φ(r) ρ/(1+rρ) dr with φ decreasing. In particular, the Schatten p-quasinorms are p-subadditive for 0<p<1, both for all n and for the full sum. This predates Rotfel'd and McCarthy (1967) by about 14 years. It uses essentially the determinant-plus-integral-representation proof later found in Seiler–Simon and Simon's Trace Ideals.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority and history point for the Rotfel'd/McCarthy inequality and the quasi-Banach structure of S_p (p<1). That structure is central to Grothendieck–Pietsch eigenvalue-distribution theory and to the theory of p-nuclear operators.

missed.claim: On the next page Grothendieck asks for a characterization of all f such that the truncated sums Σ_{i≤n} f(s_i(·)) are subadditive for every n. He also proposes a generalization to functions of several arguments. The concave case was later settled (Thompson; Uchiyama; Bourin–Uchiyama), but his explicit multivariate question is not a standard thread.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly answered (concavity with f(0)=0 suffices). The several-variable version, relating joint singular-value functionals to subadditivity, is less standard and of minor interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, complete, essentially modern proof of Rotfel'd-type subadditivity and of the S_p p-triangle inequality for p<1, about 14 years before the published credits. The method is the one later popularized by Seiler–Simon. The result is now standard, and Grothendieck may have used it implicitly in published work, so the novelty is mainly one of priority.

'φ(r) = −φ'(r)' is presumably 'φ(r) = −ψ'(r)', with ψ decreasing and vanishing at b, i.e. the intended statement is that φ is an integral of a positive measure.
